name: fhir-r4
label: HL7 FHIR R4
description: Healthcare resources — US/EU/AU government mandated standard

table_notes.patient: Demographic and administrative record for an individual receiving care; maps to FHIR Patient resource.
table_notes.practitioner: Licensed healthcare professional who provides or participates in patient care; maps to FHIR Practitioner resource.
table_notes.organization: Healthcare provider institution (hospital, clinic, lab, payer) responsible for delivering services.
table_notes.encounter: A clinical interaction between patient and provider; the central linking record for most clinical events.
table_notes.observation: Measurements and simple clinical assessments (vitals, lab results, social history) coded with LOINC or SNOMED CT.
table_notes.condition: Diagnosed problem or clinical finding recorded against a patient; coded with ICD-10 or SNOMED CT.
table_notes.medication_request: Prescriber-issued order for a medication, including dosage instructions; coded with RxNorm.
table_notes.diagnostic_report: Structured result report (labs, imaging, pathology) linking observations to a clinical interpretation.
table_notes.appointment: Scheduled future or past visit between patient and practitioner; lifecycle managed by FHIR appointment status codes.
table_notes.allergy_intolerance: Recorded allergy or adverse reaction risk for a patient; coded with NDF-RT, RxNorm, or SNOMED CT.

observation.name: id

short_description: Healthcare resources — US/EU/AU government mandated standard
long_description: HL7 FHIR R4 (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) is the definitive standard for exchanging electronic health records. Each resource type (Patient, Encounter, Observation, etc.) maps directly to a PostgreSQL table with searchable columns and a JSONB resource column for the full FHIR payload. Includes all mandatory SMART on FHIR compliance fields.
when_to_use: Use when building any clinical system that must exchange patient data with hospitals, labs, or health systems. Required by US 21st Century Cures Act (2021), EU eHDSI, NHS Digital, and ADHA (Australia). Essential for EHR integrations, patient portals, telehealth, and clinical trials.
